title: The Player Who Gives Boxes Away
logline: Night three on the floodlit pitch, but Tavi is on the bench with ice on her ankle, so Chalk sits down on the concrete and draws sixteen dots. She plays the game the way everyone plays it, grabs every box, leads three–nil and loses three–six. Dots and Boxes looks like a grabbing game. It is a giving game: whoever has to give away the big chain loses. Three chapters: the safe lines and the chains they leave behind, the all-but-two trick that keeps control, and the early gift that decides who opens the first long chain. The last game she plays second, gives two boxes on purpose, and wins six–three. A computer has played every game on this board: the second player always wins it. Next time someone says 'you go first': smile, say thank you.

characters.name: Tavi (the player, spoken to only as 'you')
characters.design: As episodes 1 and 2. New: sitBench (one boot off, ice pack on the left ankle), a chalk stub in her hand, face surprised (eyes grow) at the early gift, wince at the decline, happy at the end. Her lines and rings are teal.
characters.role: The viewer's stand-in. Grabs every box in the cold open and loses 3-6. Learns the two halves, the double-cross and the early gift. Plays second in the last game and wins 6-3.

characters.name: Chalk (the keeper made of pitch paint)
characters.design: As before: chalk-white, mittens, one eyebrow. New: sitFloor (cross-legged on the concrete), a finger that leaves chalk dots, a sleeve wipe. He hands Tavi a piece of himself to draw with. His lines and crosses are chalk white. Face flat all night; smug for the first eyebrow; thinking when she declines; surprised at the end.
characters.role: The problem-setter and the giver. Never speaks. Gives one box early in the first game and takes six in a row. In the last game he goes first and loses with the eyebrow up.

characters.name: The board (motif)
characters.design: DotsBoard: sixteen chalk dots on dark concrete, lines handwritten with a trim path, a ring for Tavi and a cross for Chalk, chains highlighted in soft orange with a chalk bow when they are a gift, safe lines shown as dashed lime ghosts, a Readout of safe lines left.
characters.role: Every line on screen is a real move from research/ep3/games.json (g1 greedy loss, g5 perfect win, g3 the eat-all branch).

characters.name: The two-halves bar (motif)
characters.design: A chalk bar under the board: the quiet half in lime, the giving half in orange, a gap mark where the safe lines run out.
characters.role: Shows that the game has two halves and where the early gift moves the turn.

Berlekamp's long chain rule (The Dots and Boxes Game, 2000; quoted in Science News): make dots + eventual long chains even if you play first, odd if second. Long chain = 3 boxes or more (Ferguson, UCLA). Fact-check wording.
